intro: Chopin’s Waltz in D♭ major, Op. 64 No. 1, known as the Minute Waltz, opens with a figure turning on a few notes before a longer melodic phrase enters. Olga Gurevich recorded it for Musopen’s Set Chopin Free project.

sections.label: A · Quavers around A♭
sections.mNote: Four bars for the right hand alone

sections.label: B · Sostenuto melody over waltz bass
sections.mNote: Long notes over the continuing waltz bass

sections.label: A′ · Trill and circling quavers
sections.mNote: The right hand plays alone before the bass re-enters.

sections.label: Coda · Descending scale to D♭
sections.mNote: A high leap begins the final descending run

cues.title: Opening, right hand alone
cues.text: The right hand circles A♭, dipping to G♮ and rising to B♭, and plays alone for four bars. The left hand then enters with the waltz accompaniment, a low bass note followed by two chords, while the right-hand figure continues.

cues.title: Recording, Musopen’s Set Chopin Free
cues.text: Olga Gurevich’s performance belongs to Musopen’s Set Chopin Free project. Musopen has released the recording into the public domain, so anyone may copy it, teach with it or pass it on.
cues.evidence: The recording’s source and public-domain dedication: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chopin_-_Waltz_No._6_in_D-flat_major,_Op._64,_No._1_'Minute'_(Olga_Gurevich).flac

cues.title: Return of the opening figure
cues.text: The circling quavers return unaccompanied. The left hand enters forte at bar 78, and three bars later the opening tune rises above the quavers again.
cues.evidence: Peters edition, bars 74–85: unaccompanied return, forte at bar 78, rising figure at bar 81. https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=483

composer.born: 1 March 1810 by his family’s reckoning; the parish register gives 22 February, Żelazowa Wola, Duchy of Warsaw
composer.epithet: Composer for the piano, known for music that drew on operatic singing and on the irregular accents of the mazurka.
facts: Wojciech Żywny; composition with Józef Elsner in Warsaw, 1826–29
Warsaw · Paris from 1831 · summers at Nohant
Piano lessons, publishing and occasional concerts
The piano, from a few lines of mazurka to concertos and sonatas
composer.background:
In February 1832 Chopin, a twenty-one-year-old Polish pianist, played in the Pleyel rooms in Paris. He had arrived the previous autumn, with two concertos behind him. The concert caught the attention of the city’s publishers, and teaching soon supplied his living. For the rest of his life his profession depended on people hearing him at close quarters. The great public virtuosos travelled from one concert city to the next; Chopin stayed in Paris and gave lessons.

He was born at Żelazowa Wola in 1810. His father, Nicolas, had come from France and worked as a tutor; his mother, Justyna Krzyżanowska, was Polish. The family moved to Warsaw while Fryderyk was still a baby, when Nicolas obtained a teaching post at the Lyceum. At seven the boy had a polonaise in print. Wojciech Żywny taught him the piano, with Bach and Mozart among his models; Józef Elsner later gave him a rigorous training in composition at Warsaw’s Main School of Music.
